args.flag_of_other_command: --{flag} is not a flag of {command}; it belongs to ocho {owner}
args.out_of_range: --{flag} {value} is not a whole number from {min} to {max}
args.next: Run ocho help for the list of commands and global flags.
args.next_command: Run ocho help {command} for its flags and examples.
error.data.during_read: nothing was changed; the read was incomplete
error.data.file_write: the broker was not touched; {file} is unchanged
error.internal: internal error: {detail}. This is a bug in Ocho.
error.internal.next: Please open an issue and attach: ocho doctor --save snapshot.json --redact-hosts (Ocho {tool}, Node {node}, {os})
file.invalid: {file} has {count, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}}
file.invalid.next: Fix the listed lines in {file}, or run with --no-file.
contexts.invalid.next: Fix {file} by hand, or remove it and add the contexts again with ocho context add.
target.none.next: Pass --url and --user, set OCHO_URL, or add a context: ocho context add prod --url https://host:15671 --user ocho-doctor
target.unknown_context.next: Run ocho context list, or add it with ocho context add.
target.user_missing.next: Pass --user or set OCHO_USER together with --url.
target.url_wins: --url is set, so context {context} is ignored
doctor.estimate: Reading {queues} queues: about {requests} requests, ~{duration}. Ctrl-C stops safely; nothing is written.
doctor.flow_needs_file: --flow {flow} needs ocho.yaml, and none was found
doctor.target_version_invalid: --target-version {value} is not a version; write it as major.minor, for example 4.2
doctor.target_version_not_newer: --target-version {target} is not newer than the broker version {version}
report.unchecked_s1: {count, plural, one {# result of an S1 rule was} other {# results of S1 rules were}} not checked, so this does not mean safe.
explain.missing_target: explain needs a target: a rule code, a code, or queue|exchange|flow <name>
explain.unknown_kind: {kind} is not queue, exchange or flow
explain.not_found_any: no queue or exchange {name} in vhost {vhost}, and {name} is not a known code
explain.ambiguous: both a queue and an exchange are named {name} in vhost {vhost}; write ocho explain queue {name} or ocho explain exchange {name}
explain.flow_needs_file: explain flow needs ocho.yaml, and none was found
explain.caught_by.client: client code; not visible from the broker
explain.broker.unverified: Not verified: the broker does not report effective_policy_definition
context.missing_sub: context needs a subcommand: add, use, list, show or remove
context.unknown_sub_near: unknown subcommand context {sub}; did you mean {near}?
context.saved_current: Saved context {name} in {file}; it is now the current context.
context.none: No contexts in {file}. Add one with ocho context add.
context.col.name: NAME
context.remove_needs_yes: stdin is not a terminal; pass --yes to remove context {name}
import.bad_definitions: {file} is not a RabbitMQ definitions file: {detail}
import.topology_unknown: the topology cannot be read completely: {collections} unknown
import.topology_unknown.next: Give the user read access to every vhost (monitoring tag), or import from a definitions export with --from.
import.auto_non_interactive.stdin: stdin is not a terminal: running non-interactively; every flow stays undeclared.
import.auto_non_interactive.json: --json is set: running non-interactively; every flow stays undeclared.
import.family: Family proposal {i}/{total}: {template}  ({count, plural, one {# member} other {# members}}: {members})
import.family_help: Accept writes one family with a name template instead of one flow per queue; doctor then checks every member the same way. Skip keeps the queues as separate flows.
import.param_invalid: {param} is not a valid parameter name: use a-z, 0-9 and _, starting with a letter.
import.member_help: Add puts the new queue in the family member list, so doctor checks it like the others. Skip leaves the list as it is.
import.tolerance_choices: [s]trict  [l]oose  [k]eep undeclared  [A]pply to the rest of this exchange  [?] [k] >
import.tolerance_help: strict: a message lost in this flow is an S1 finding. loose: losing a message here is acceptable. undeclared: not decided yet; doctor checks only structure.
import.apply_rest: Tolerance for the rest of this exchange [s/l/k] >
import.eof: stdin closed in the middle of the questions; nothing was written
import.eof.next: Answer every question, or run ocho import --non-interactive.
import.below_min_version: The broker runs RabbitMQ {actual}, below broker.min_version {min} in ocho.yaml.
import.unchanged: {file} is up to date; nothing to write. Next: ocho doctor
import.wrote: Wrote {file}: {flows, plural, one {# flow} other {# flows}} ({strict} strict, {loose} loose, {undeclared} undeclared), {families, plural, one {# family} other {# families}}, {unmanaged, plural, one {# unmanaged object} other {# unmanaged objects}}. Next: ocho doctor
help.more: Run ocho help <command> for the flags and examples of one command.
help.read_only: Read-only: this command never writes to the broker.
help.ocho.purpose: ocho reads a RabbitMQ broker and tells you where messages can be lost.
help.doctor.purpose: Read the broker, check every rule, and print what to fix first.
help.import.purpose: Write ocho.yaml from the broker topology, asking the tolerance of each flow.
help.explain.purpose: Explain a rule, a code, or where each effective value of an object comes from.
help.context.purpose: Manage saved brokers: add, use, list, show, remove.
help.context.usage: ocho context add <name> --url <url> --user <user> [--password-command <cmd>] | use <name> | list | show [<name>] | remove <name>
help.context.example1: ocho context add prod --url https://b-1.mq.example:443 --user ocho-doctor --password-command "op read op://infra/rabbit/password"
help.help.purpose: Print help for ocho or one command.
help.flag.global.url: Broker URL without a context (OCHO_URL); goes with --user
help.flag.global.password-stdin: Read the password from the first line of stdin
help.flag.global.prometheus-url: Prometheus URL instead of the detected one
help.flag.doctor.flow: Check only the objects of this flow (needs ocho.yaml)
help.flag.doctor.target-version: Add the upgrade rules for this RabbitMQ version
help.flag.doctor.fail-on: Lowest severity that makes the exit code 1 (default S1)
help.flag.doctor.file: ocho.yaml to use (default ./ocho.yaml if it exists)
help.flag.doctor.no-file: Ignore ocho.yaml; every flow is undeclared
help.flag.doctor.save: Save a snapshot of what was read (.gz to compress)
help.flag.doctor.redact-hosts: Replace host and connection names in the snapshot
help.flag.doctor.from: Check a snapshot instead of a broker
help.flag.doctor.why: Show the mechanism for S2 and S3 too
help.flag.doctor.verbose: Show every object and every S4, S5 finding
help.flag.import.from: Read the topology from a definitions export instead of a broker
help.flag.import.non-interactive: Ask nothing: flows stay undeclared, family proposals are skipped
help.flag.context.password-command: Command whose first output line is the password (context add)
help.flag.context.yes: Do not ask before removing (context remove)
